title: Parallax MENDALA — Publication Pack 1
description: Source-led public briefs and evidence-safe vector diagrams for the full-size and portable MENDALA product families.

projects.tagline: A modular, observable growing-system family spanning portable learning units, household systems, and community foodwheels.
projects.story: Parallax MENDALA—Modular Ecological Nutrient Delivery & Autonomous Living Agriculture—organizes water, light, air, roots, sensing, maintenance, and human authority into a six-petal system pattern. The architecture spans the full-size MENDALA-24, 48, 108, and 216 family and the portable Seed-6, Go-18, and Go XL-36 family. Publication Pack 1 makes the design basis inspectable while keeping physical performance claims behind measured prototype receipts.
projects.summary: MENDALA is the first Parallax physical-product record with a published family map, system poster, prototype proof path, cost-planning boundary, and source-led architecture briefs. MENDALA-108 remains the reference full-size configuration, while Go-18 remains the first serious portable prototype target.
projects.see: The six-petal architecture, full-size and portable family maps, documented portable cost-planning bands, the dual-loop water-bench proof, and the staged path from Go-18 to MENDALA-48 and later reference-scale engineering.
projects.proof: Seven public artifacts are now connected: three reviewed SVG diagrams and four browser-readable briefs derived from two retained canonical DOCX specifications. This proves the publication package, not the agricultural performance. No physical water-bench, Go-18, MENDALA-48, yield, durability, or commercial-economics receipt is yet published.
projects.next: Build and instrument the dual-loop water bench; publish flow, leak, conditioning, uptime, maintenance, shutdown, and repair receipts; then use those findings to construct the Go-18 portable prototype and MENDALA-48 fixed pilot.
projects.claimBoundary: MENDALA remains a design-stage physical product family. The published visuals and briefs explain architecture and planning assumptions; they do not validate crop yield, monthly output, durability, food safety, emergency certification, final cost, manufacturing readiness, or commercial viability. The documented cost figures are planning bands, not retail quotes.
